release_name: Offline boot and updates that actually land
notes: Two service-worker fixes, both proven in a real browser with a real service worker rather than a mock. (1) modules/feastdoc.js is a static top-level import of app.js and render.js but was never in the CORE precache list, so offline the module 408s, app.js never evaluates, and the app renders its HTML shell with ZERO Masses while looking like it loaded. Demonstrated end to end: clean install, server stopped, reload gave 0 cards and a failed app.js import; with feastdoc.js added to CORE the same test gives 60 cards and 387 results. (2) The install handler used cache.addAll(CORE) with default cache mode, so a new worker precached whatever the browser HTTP cache already held. GitHub Pages serves every asset with Cache-Control: max-age=600 (verified against the live site), while the update CHECK deliberately bypasses that cache (version.json?ts= with no-store). That asymmetry means the banner appears the instant a release is deployed but the assets cannot be fetched fresh for another ten minutes, so the new worker installs the OLD app, the page reloads unchanged and the banner reappears - which is exactly the failed in-app update reported from the device. Reproduced exactly: updating 27.6.6 to 27.6.7 left the app on 27.6.6 with the banner still showing and the new cache holding the old index.html. With addAll now issuing Request(u,{cache:reload}), the same test updates 27.6.7 to 27.6.8 correctly: running version 27.6.8, banner cleared, stale cache deleted, all 25 CORE entries fresh. The fix is self-applying: the install handler that runs during an update belongs to the NEW worker, so an existing stuck install repairs itself on its first update to this version. No data change: 417 rows, 120 sites.
